text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Justice minister, religious party head and Prime Minister Netanyahu's director general could be charged over short-lived appointment of attorney general last month.
- Minister signs work permit to build Jewish neighbourhood in Arab East Jerusalem.
- Palestinian President Arafat could ask Clinton to press Israel to rescind East Jerusalem building plan.
- Holocaust survivors prominent on Swiss fund board.

- Treasury increasingly concerned at local bidders ongoing failure to win government tenders offered by European Union countries; Israel unhappy at lack of market access and proliferation of non-tariff barriers.
- Tecnomatix Tehcnologies Ltd software company gets order for its Robcad/spot software from Subaru; refused to give value of deal.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu lawyer calls for police who leaked information to be taken off investigation into attorney general affair.
- Netanyahu's director general, interrogated in attorney general affair, tells Russian magazine: There is a whole group of journalists who should go.
- Secret report says air force officers tried to wreck investigation into death of soldier playing with airplane cable in 1992.
- Transport minister plans to give city supervisors authority to act as traffic police.
- Minister signs order to build in Arab East Jerusalem.
MAARIV
- Good possibility of charges against Justice minister, religious party politician and Netanyahu's director general.
- Teacher denies raping girl, 14.
- Bank strike today; they'll strike also on Tuesday.
- Preparedness against unrest over building in Arab East Jerusalem.
- Rival newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth sent private investigators to go through Maariv's garbage, investigator testifies.
- Interview with Nelson Mandela on his upcoming trip to Israel.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu and Internal Security Minister attack police in wake of leaks on attorney general affair.
- Teacher says girl, 14, agreed to sex.
- Minister signs order to build in East Jerusalem.
- Commander of army air base delays civilian plane landing so he can take off.
- Interview with Jordan's King Hussein: Netanyahu will not fall.
- Pop star Madonna is studying Kabala ancient Jewish lore.
GLOBES
- Three ministers were urged by other ministers to accept short-lived appointment of attorney general last month.
- Steep fall of 64.5 percent in Bank of Israel revenues from excess foreign currency investment in 1996.
